==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|stā}}, {{IPA|en|/steɪ/}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-stay.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ste/|a=Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/stei/|a=Wales,non-pain-pane}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪ|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|steyen}}, {{m|enm|staien}}, from {{der|en|fro|estayer}}, {{m|fro|estaier||to fix, prop up, support, stay}}, from {{m|fro|estaye}}, {{m|fro|estaie||a prop, stay}}, from {{der|en|dum|staeye||a prop, stay}}, a contracted form of {{m|dum|staede}}, {{m|dum|stade|t=a prop, stay, help, aid}} (compare {{cog|dum|staeyen}}, {{m|dum|staeden||to make firm, stay, support, hold still, stabilise}}), from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*stadi||a site, place, location, standing}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*stadiz||a standing, place}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*stéh₂tis||standing}}. Influenced by {{cog|ang|stæġ}} {{gloss|"a stay, rope"; see below}}. Cognate with {{cog|ang|stede||a place, spot, locality, fixed position, station, site, standing, status, position of a moving body, stopping, standing still, stability, fixity, firmness, steadfastness}}, {{cog|sv|stödja||to prop, support, brace, hold up, bolster}}, {{cog|is|stöðug||continuous, stable}}. More at {{l|en|stead}}, {{l|en|steady}}. Sense of "remain, continue" may be due to later influence from {{cog|fro|ester}}, {{m|fro|esteir||to stand, be, continue, remain}}, from {{cog|la|stāre||stand}}, from the same Proto-Indo-European root above; however, derivation from this root is untenable based on linguistic and historical grounds.Whitney, ''Century Dictionary and Encyclopedia'', stay. An alternative etymology derives {{der|en|fro|estaye}}, {{m|fro|estaie}}, from {{der|en|frk|*stakā}}, {{m|frk|*stakō||t=stake, post}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*stakô||stake, bar, stick, pole}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)teg-||rod, pole, stick}}, making it cognate with {{cog|ang|staca||pin, stake}}, {{cog|ang|stician||to stick, be placed, lie, remain fixed}}. Cognate with Albanian {{m|sq|shtagë||a long stick, a pole}}. More at {{l|en|stake}}, {{l|en|stick}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|+|+|+,staid}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[remain]] in a particular place, especially for a [[definite]] or short period of time; [[sojourn]]; [[abide]]. #: {{ux|en|We '''stayed''' in Hawaii for a week.  I can only '''stay''' for an hour.}} #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|1|10|page=140|text=She would commaund the hasty Sunne to '''stay''',
Or backward turne his course from heuen's hight,}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Spanish Fryar|page=60|text='''Stay''', I command you; '''stay''' and hear me first,}} #* '''1874''' {{w|Henry Wadsworth Longfellow}}, “Three Friends of Mine,” IV, in ''The Masque of Pandora and Other Poems'', Boston: James R. Osgood, 1875, p.{{nbsp}}353,[https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008655872] #* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=5|passage=“Well,” I says, “I cal'late a body could get used to Tophet if he '''stayed''' there long enough.” ¶ She flared up; the least mite of a slam at Doctor Wool was enough to set her going.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|copulative}} To [[continue]] to have a particular [[quality]]. #: {{ux|en|Wear gloves so your hands '''stay''' warm.}} #: {{ux|en|Promise me you'll always '''stay'''/remain my little prince.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|chapter=Meleager and Atalanta|page=118|passage=For as the Flames augment, and as they '''stay''' / At their full Height, then languish to decay, / They rise, and sink by Fits {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Alcott Little Women|part=2|chapter=XXX|passage=The evergreen arch wouldn’t '''stay''' firm after she got it up, but wiggled and threatened to tumble down on her head when the hanging baskets were filled.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1943|author=w:Graham Greene|title=w:The Ministry of Fear|location=London|publisher=Heinemann|year_published=1960|section=Book 3, Chapter 2, p. 210|url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.225974 |passage=The three men in the room '''stayed''' motionless, holding their breaths.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-21|author=w:Oliver Burkeman| volume=189| issue=2| page=27| magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly| title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2013/may/10/conscious-computing-twitter-facebook-google The tao of tech]| passage=The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you "'''stay''' up to date with what your friends are doing",{{...}}and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[prop]]; [[support]]; [[sustain]]; [[hold up]]; [[steady]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|III|7|text=''Lord Mayor of London''. See, where he stands between two clergymen!
''Duke of Buckingham''. Two props of virtue for a Christian prince,
To '''stay''' him from the fall of vanity:}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Exodus|17|12|text=But Moses hands were heavy; and they took a stone, and put it under him, and he sat thereon; and Aaron and Hur '''stayed''' up his hands, the one on the one side, and the other on the other side; and his hands were steady until the going down of the sun.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1677|author=w:Hannah Woolley|title=The Compleat Servant-Maid|location=London|publisher=T. Passinger|chapter=Directions for Writing the most Vsual and Legible Hands for Women|page=17|url=http://name.umdl.umich.edu/A66839.0001.001 |passage=Draw in your right elbow, turn your hand outward and bear it lightly, gripe not the pen too hard, with your left hand '''stay''' the paper.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1725|translator=w:John Dryden|title={{w|Virgil}}’s Husbandry, or an Essay on the {{w|Georgics}}|location=London|section=Book 2, p. 37|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/001810665 |passage=Sallows and Reeds, on Banks of Rivers born,
Remain to cut; for Vineyards useful found,
To '''stay''' thy Vines and fence thy fruitful Ground.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To support from sinking; to sustain with strength; to satisfy in part or for the time. #* {{RQ:Scott Woodstock|chapter=20|text={{...}} he has devoured a whole loaf of bread and butter, as fast as Phoebe could cut it, and it has not '''staid''' his stomach for a minute {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[stop]] or [[delay]] something. ## To [[stop]]; [[detain]]; keep back; [[delay]]; [[hinder]]. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|IV|2|text=Your ships are '''stay’d''' at Venice.}} ##* '''1671''', {{w|John Evelyn}}, ''{{w|John Evelyn's Diary|Diary}}'', entry dated 14{{nbsp}}November, 1671, in ''The Diary of John Evelyn'', London: Macmillan, 1906, Volume 2, p.{{nbsp}}337,[https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/007694262] ##*: This business '''staid''' me in London almost a week {{...}} ##* {{RQ:Locke Human Understanding|chapter=5|page=207|text={{...}} I was willing to '''stay''' my Reader on an Argument, that appears to me new {{...}}}} ##* {{RQ:Dickens Tale of Two Cities|chapter=6|text=The task of recalling him from the vagrancy into which he always sank when he had spoken, was like recalling some very weak person from a swoon, or endeavouring, in the hope of some disclosure, to '''stay''' the spirit of a fast-dying man.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1925|author=w:Virginia Woolf|title=w:Mrs. Dalloway|publisher=Harcourt Brace Jovanovich|year_published=1985|page=44|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/mrsdalloway000wool |passage={{...}} she filled the room she entered, and felt often as she stood hesitating one moment on the threshold of her drawing-room, an exquisite suspense, such as might '''stay''' a diver before plunging while the sea darkens and brightens beneath him {{...}}}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2010|author=w:Howard Jacobson|title=w:The Finkler Question|chapter=9|publisher=Bloomsbury|location=New York |passage=She rose to leave but Libor '''stayed''' her.}} ## To [[restrain]]; [[withhold]]; [[check]]; stop. ##* '''1597''', {{w|Richard Hooker}}, ''Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity'', Book 5, in ''The Works of Mr. Richard Hooker'', London: Andrew Crook, 1666, p.{{nbsp}},[http://name.umdl.umich.edu/A44334.0001.001] ##*: {{...}} all that may but with any the least shew of possibility '''stay''' their mindes from thinking that true, which they heartily wish were false, but cannot think it so {{...}} ##* {{RQ:KJV|1 Samuel|24|7|text=So David '''stayed''' his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul.}} ##* '''1852''', {{w|Charlotte Brontë}}, letter cited in {{w|Elizabeth Gaskell}}, ''{{w|The Life of Charlotte Brontë}}'', 1857, Volume 2, Chapter{{nbsp}}10,[http://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/1700/pg1700-images.html] ##*: {{...}} you must follow the impulse of your own inspiration. If THAT commands the slaying of the victim, no bystander has a right to put out his hand to '''stay''' the sacrificial knife: but I hold you a stern priestess in these matters. ##* {{RQ:Dunsany Pegana||23|Between Pegāna and the Earth flutter ten thousand thousand prayers that beat their wings against the face of Death, and never for one of them hath the hand of the Striker been '''stayed''', nor yet have tarried the feet of the Relentless One.}} ## To cause to [[cease]]; to put an end to. ##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Titus|III|1|text=Now '''stay''' your strife {{...}}}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1847|author=w:Ralph Waldo Emerson|chapter=Threnody|title=Poems|location=Boston|publisher=James Munroe|page=242|url=https://archive.org/details/poems1847emer |passage=For flattering planets seemed to say
This child should ills of ages '''stay''',}} ## To [[put off]]; [[defer]]; [[postpone]]; delay; keep back. ##: {{ux|en|The governor '''stayed''' the execution until the appeal could be heard.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1935|author=w:Pearl S. Buck|title={{w|A House Divided (novel)|A House Divided}}|location=London|publisher=Methuen|section=Part 1, p. 137|url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.40679 |passage=Without one word to deny himself, Yuan let himself be bound, his hands behind his back, and no one could '''stay''' the matter.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=w:Richard Flanagan|title={{w|Gould's Book of Fish|Gould’s Book of Fish}}|location=New York|publisher=Grove|chapter=The Leatherjacket|pages=187–188|url=https://openlibrary.org/ia/gouldsbookoffish00flan |passage=As I curled up like a dying fish beneath his flailing boots, I managed to '''stay''' his assault long enough to tell him that I had only ever seen myself as his most loyal servant {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To hold the attention of. {{rfquote-sense|en}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To bear up under; to endure; to hold out against; to resist. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Romeo and Juliet|I|1|text=She will not '''stay''' the siege of loving terms,
Nor bide the encounter of assailing eyes,}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[wait]] for; [[await]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Two Gentlemen of Verona|II|2|text=My father '''stays''' my coming;}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|III|2|text=Let me '''stay''' the growth of his beard,}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To remain for the purpose of; to stay to take part in or be present at (a meal, ceremony etc.). #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 3|III|2|text=I '''stay''' dinner there.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1791|author=w:Elizabeth Inchbald|title=A Simple Story|page=177|publisher=Oxford|year_published=2009 |passage=Some of the company '''staid''' supper, which prevented the embarrassment that must unavoidably have arisen, had the family been by themselves.}} #* {{RQ:Austen Persuasion|chapter=7|text=How glad they had been to hear papa invite him to '''stay''' dinner, how sorry when he said it was quite out of his power {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[rest]];
